bodyParagraphs: NASA says the NICER telescope on the space station has stopped its science work. It launched in 2017. It studied neutron stars with X-rays. Engineers think a motor inside failed. They plan to finish the data archive. They will remove the telescope later.

articles.headline: NOAA: October 2026 Was Very Warm
bodyParagraphs: NOAA says October 2026 was very warm. The global surface temperature was 1.43 degrees Celsius above the twentieth-century average. This is the highest monthly departure in the 1850 to 2026 record. It is a global average, not every local place. All ten of the warmest Octobers have happened since 2015.

vocabulary.definitionEn: a number that represents the whole world together
the amount something is different from the usual level

articles.headline: NASA Ends NICER Telescope Science Work on Space Station
bodyParagraphs: NASA says the NICER telescope on the International Space Station has stopped its science work. The instrument launched in 2017 to study neutron stars using X-ray light. Engineers believe an internal motor has failed. They plan to finish the data archive and later remove the telescope from the station. The mission lasted much longer than the first eighteen-month plan. Scientists will still use the collected data for new research.

vocabulary.definitionEn: a small engine inside a machine that makes parts move

articles.headline: NASA Ends NICER Telescope Science Work on Space Station
bodyParagraphs: NASA reports that the NICER telescope on the International Space Station has ended its science work. The instrument launched in 2017 and studied neutron stars using X-ray light. Engineers believe an internal motor failed inside the device. They are now planning to finish the data archive and remove the telescope from the station. The motor problem is still an assessment and not a confirmed diagnosis. Removal is a future plan and has not happened yet. NICER completed its main mission and gave scientists valuable information about dense stars. The telescope operated for several years beyond its original schedule.

vocabulary.definitionEn: a careful judgement based on available information
identifying the nature or cause of a problem

articles.headline: NIST Lab Test Uses Light Particles to Check a Distant Location
bodyParagraphs: NIST researchers demonstrated a laboratory method that uses light particles to check a distant party's location. The team sends entangled photons, or linked light particles, through optical fibers to measure position securely. Researchers developed this new protocol in a laboratory. Scientists say the approach could help protect private information in future networks. However, real-world use may be a decade or more away. The experiment remains in a controlled lab setting. It is not an available security product for consumers today. The result shows a laboratory possibility, rather than a service people can buy.

vocabulary.definitionEn: light particles with strongly linked measurement results
very thin glass threads that guide light signals

articles.headline: Library of Congress Plans New Exhibition on Indigenous History
bodyParagraphs: The Library of Congress plans to open a new permanent exhibition on November 19, 2026. The display is called Voices of the Early Americas and will be located in the Thomas Jefferson Building. It explores Indigenous histories, cultures, and enduring traditions through over 200 objects. The materials span more than 3,000 years and include maps, manuscripts, photographs, and a Maya wooden box. Contemporary poetry is also featured to show living traditions. The exhibition uses rare artifacts to tell a long story of the Americas. Visitors can see how Indigenous peoples have shaped the continent for millennia.

vocabulary.definitionEn: lasting for a long time; continuing to exist
periods of one thousand years each

articles.headline: NOAA Compares October Temperatures With a Twentieth-Century Reference
bodyParagraphs: NOAA reports that October 2026 was warmer than the twentieth-century average. The global surface temperature reached 1.43 degrees Celsius above the twentieth-century average. These measurements use a specific reference period to make the temperature comparison. The data comes from NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information. All ten of the warmest Octobers have occurred since 2015. NOAA's figures describe a global average, not identical conditions in every location. The baseline used is the twentieth-century average, not preindustrial levels. The report places October's temperature in context by comparing it with a long-term reference.

vocabulary.definitionEn: a set period used as a standard for comparison
describing the period before large-scale industrial development
